q: What is ds-ch-ab-wave1 in the collections-channel-mix project, and what did it test?
a: Wave 1 is the Jul-Aug 2025 randomised test of SMS, call, email and control on 1-29 DPD accounts. It had n=86,000 (SMS 28,400, call 28,300, email 14,500, control 14,800).

q: What came of exp-503 in the collections-channel-mix project?
a: Email lifted promise-to-pay only 0.3pp (6.4% against 6.1%, CI -1.1 to +1.7). That led to find-ch-email-no-lift, and dec-ch-email-drop removed email from the 1-29 DPD contact plan on 2025-09-12.

q: What does ch-propensity-v2 in the collections-channel-mix project use as inputs?
a: ch-propensity-v2 uses feat-ch-send-window-v1, feat-ch-prior-contact-v1 and feat-ch-prefer-channel-v1. feat-ch-email-open-v1 is excluded.

q: What is the current channel-choice model in the collections-channel-mix project?
a: ch-propensity-v2, dated 2025-11-18, which replaced ch-propensity-v1. The ch-bandit-v1 allocator is simulated but not promoted.

q: What is the wave-2 promise-to-pay lift for SMS-only and for call-first on 8-29 DPD in the collections-channel-mix project?
a: SMS-only lifts promise-to-pay 3.1pp (8.1% against 5.0% control, n=18,000) and call-first lifts it 5.9pp (10.9%, n=17,700), so SMS captures about 53% of the call lift (exp-504).

q: Why was the wave-1 claim that SMS captures about 80% of the call lift overturned in the collections-channel-mix project?
a: Wave 2 on 8-29 DPD found SMS-only captured 53% of the call lift (3.1pp against 5.9pp). find-ch-sms-call-gap superseded find-ch-sms-matches-call, and the team adopted SMS-then-call escalation.
